title: Schwarzschild radius
references: Schwarzschild, K., On the gravitational field of a mass point according to Einstein's theory (English translation by S. Antoci and A. Loinger of Sitzungsberichte der Koeniglich Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften 1916, 189-196), arXiv:physics/9905030, doi:10.48550/arXiv.physics/9905030
Misner, C. W., Thorne, K. S. and Wheeler, J. A., Gravitation, W. H. Freeman (1973)
validity_domain: Radius of the event horizon of a non-rotating, uncharged mass M in vacuum (Schwarzschild solution of general relativity): r_s = 2 G M / c^2. The claim is the radius in the Schwarzschild coordinate, the circumference divided by 2 pi.
limitations: Non-rotating and uncharged: a rotating (Kerr) or charged black hole has a different horizon radius
The formula gives the horizon radius for a black hole; it does not say that a given body is one, and it is not the radius of a star or planet
The uncertainty of G (CODATA 2022) is propagated by the engine, apart from the tolerance
The mass is in kg or g; no solar-mass unit is in the core units table
